title: Toward SLM-based agentic task-tool intent matching
abstract: Tool-equipped AI agents use tool calls to access data and act on external systems. The study investigates Small Language Models as task-tool relevance classifiers that independently evaluate selected tools against an assigned task and returns a relevance signal for downstream enforcement. It introduces a multi-tool dataset spanning distinct MCP servers and applies prompt optimization, supervised fine-tuning, and GRPO to specialize SLMs.
notes: Authoritative arXiv metadata and full PDF were inspected on 2026-10-06. The paper reports 352 tools across 12 MCP servers, server-disjoint validation/test pools, Gemma 3 1B and 4B, sequential Base→GEPA→SFT→GRPO optimization, and a 95% accuracy/F1 operational target. The paper links author code/data, but that repository was not available through the current GitHub access path at verification time, so no author artifacts are copied or relied upon.
